source.title: Parent execution stays `waiting` forever when its sub-execution finishes during the parked-parent sweep and the child's row is already deleted

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Bug Description

A parent execution waiting on a sub-workflow (Execute Workflow, "wait for sub-workflow completion") stayed `waiting` for about 12 hours after the child finished successfully, until I stopped it by hand. Nothing errored. The two resume paths in `WaitTracker` each left the parent to the other one:

1. The child finished (it had resumed from a Wait node, so it went through `WaitTracker.startExecution` → `resumeParentExecution`). `patchParent` succeeded, then `claimParent` → `startExecution(parent)` threw `ExecutionAlreadyResumingError`, because the 60 s `resumeParentsOfFinishedSubExecutions` sweep was holding the parent in `this.resuming` at that moment. `claimParent` does not retry that error. It logs and returns, expecting the sweep to pick the parent up:
   ```
   2026-11-21T05:09:44.981Z Parent execution not claimable: already claimed by another process, or not parked yet
   ```
2. The sub-workflow has `saveDataSuccessExecution: "none"`, so the child's row was deleted as soon as it finished. The sweep's `patchParentWithFinishedChild` finds no row for the parent's `waitingChildExecutionIds`, logs, and returns without claiming:
   ```
   2026-11-21T05:09:44.992Z Parent execution waits on sub-executions that no longer exist
   ```
   It logs that line every minute from then on. The parent is never resumed.

The JSDoc on `claimParent` says a failed claim is picked up by `resumeParentsOfFinishedSubExecutions` on the next tick. That doesn't hold when the child's row no longer exists.

Most runs finish outside the sweep's short window. The same workflow ran fine 20 minutes earlier.

### To Reproduce

It's a timing race, so I haven't got a deterministic repro. The conditions:

1. Sub-workflow with `saveDataSuccessExecution: "none"` that contains a Wait node, so it parks and is resumed by the wait tracker.
2. Parent calls it with Execute Workflow and waits for completion.
3. The child finishes while the leader's `resumeParentsOfFinishedSubExecutions` sweep (every 60 s) is inspecting that parent, i.e. between `this.resuming.add(parentId)` and `this.resuming.delete(parentId)` in `resumeParentIfChildFinished`.

Result: the parent stays `waiting` with nothing left to resume it.

### Expected behavior

The parent resumes once with the child's result. For example, `claimParent` could retry `ExecutionAlreadyResumingError` after the other holder releases the parent. Or, since `patchParent` already wrote the child's result into the parent, the sweep could claim a patched parent even when the child row is gone.

### Debug Info

Code on this path is the same in 2.46.7 (where I hit it), 2.48.7, 2.49.3, 3.3.0 and current master: `packages/cli/src/wait-tracker.ts` (`claimParent`, `resumeParentIfChildFinished`, `patchParentWithFinishedChild`).

### Operating System
Linux (Docker image on Kubernetes)

### n8n Version
2.46.7

### Node.js Version
26.12.1

### Database
PostgreSQL

### Execution mode
main (default)

### Hosting
self hosted

comments.author: grinem
comments.text: Until this is patched upstream, the immediate unblocker is setting `saveDataSuccessExecution: "all"` on the child workflow and relying on global `EXECUTIONS_DATA_PRUNE=true` (with a short `EXECUTIONS_DATA_MAX_AGE`) so the row survives long enough for the sweep to resolve.

Thanks for the detailed report. I can reproduce the race in the code.

In claimParent() (wait-tracker.ts), ExecutionAlreadyResumingError is treated as non-retryable. When the child-completion path patches the parent, then tries to claim it while resumeParentIfChildFinished() is holding the parent in this.resuming for inspection, claimParent() logs and returns, relying on the next sweep.

That fallback breaks when saveDataSuccessExecution is "none": the child row can be deleted as soon as it finishes, so patchParentWithFinishedChild() finds no child row, logs “no longer exist”, and never claims the parent. The parent stays waiting even though its data was already patched with the child result.

I’m looking into a fix that makes this handoff deterministic—either by retrying/waiting on local resume contention, or by letting the sweep claim a parent only when it can confirm the child result was already applied.

comments.author: dvystrcil
comments.text:
Thanks @Arin004joshi for confirming the race, and @grinem for the workaround.

An update from my side. For anyone who hits this and can't keep the child's data: I couldn't use `saveDataSuccessExecution: "all"` on the sub-workflow, because its execution data holds a short-lived per-run credential that I don't want stored in Postgres, even briefly.

Instead, the parents no longer wait on a sub-execution. The parent passes `$execution.resumeUrl` to the sub-workflow, starts it with Execute Workflow (`waitForSubWorkflow: false`), and parks on a Wait node set to "On Webhook Call". The sub-workflow POSTs its result to that URL when it finishes. That avoids the `claimParent` / `resumeParentIfChildFinished` handoff completely. Since the change (2026-11-21), chains have resumed cleanly.

Either of the fixes you describe would make "wait for sub-workflow completion" safe again with `saveDataSuccessExecution: "none"`. I'm happy to test a branch against the same setup (2.46.7, PostgreSQL, main mode).

Thanks @dvystrcil for the update and for sharing the workaround. It’s a clean way to avoid the sub-execution handoff when child execution data cannot be stored.

The PR I opened ([[#44765](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/44765)](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/44765)) addresses the same race condition. When the child finishes while the leader's parked-parent sweep is inspecting the parent, `WaitTracker` now waits for the local inspection to release before retrying the parent claim. The retry is limited to `ExecutionAlreadyResumingError` caused by local contention, so existing cross-process claim behavior remains unchanged.

This should make **Wait for Sub-Workflow Completion** work reliably with `saveDataSuccessExecution: "none"` for this particular race.

There is still one separate edge case outside the scope of this fix: if the child finishes before the parent is parked and its execution record is deleted before any result can be patched into the parent, there is no result available for the sweep to apply.

Would you be willing to test the PR branch against your setup (n8n 2.46.7, PostgreSQL, main mode)? You can check out the branch locally, run the same reproduction, and verify whether the parent resumes successfully without repeatedly logging `Parent execution waits on sub-executions that no longer exist`.

Please share your findings, especially if you can still reproduce the hang. Your setup would be particularly useful for validating this fix.

comments.author: dvystrcil
comments.text:
Thanks @Arin004joshi, I'll test it.

Since the window is a single DB query, plain re-runs won't show much either way. So I'm planning a harness that makes the race repeatable: stock 2.46.7 against 2.46.7 with your change ported to the compiled `wait-tracker.js`, each with Postgres behind a latency proxy so the sweep's inspection lasts seconds. Then I'll fire a batch of parent/sub-workflow runs timed to finish inside it. I'll post the stuck-parent and log-line counts for both.

A question from reading the diff: the retry only covers `local` contention. In multi-main, the leader runs the sweep while a follower can handle the child's resume. Wouldn't that still leave the parent stuck? We run a single main, so it doesn't affect us, but it may be worth a note in the PR.

comments.author: dvystrcil
Arin004joshi
comments.text:
> Tested [#44765](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/44765) against 2.46.7 (PostgreSQL, main mode). It fixes the hang in my harness: **stock 10/90 parents stuck, patched 0/90.**
> 
> The window is one DB query wide, so plain re-runs wouldn't show anything. I put toxiproxy between n8n and Postgres with 500 ms of latency on every reply. That stretches the sweep's inspection of each parent to a few seconds. Then I fired 90 parents, one every 7 s. Each one calls a child with `saveDataSuccessExecution: "none"` and a Wait of 70–130 s. That's above the 65 s in-process threshold, so the child goes through `WaitTracker`. Both images ran at the same time with the same parameters.
> 
> n8n 2.46.7	parents `success`	parents still `waiting` 3 min after the last child was due	`Parent execution not claimable`	`waits on sub-executions that no longer exist`
> stock	80	**10**	10	111
> with [#44765](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/44765)	90	**0**	0	36
> * **Stock:** 10 `not claimable` lines and 10 stuck parents. The logs are plain text without execution IDs, so I can't pair them, but the counts match. The stuck parents presumably account for most of the 111 `no longer exist` lines, since the sweep re-inspects them every minute. (With pruning on, the child row is soft-deleted, so the sweep's `findStatusesByIds` no longer sees it.)
> * **Patched:** all 90 parents finished `success` and none stayed `waiting`. To see the new path run, I added one log line in `waitForInspectionRelease` after the `inspecting` check. That line is not in your PR. It fired 18 times, so claims did hit the sweep's inspection and waited it out instead of giving up.
> 
> I didn't build master or run the PR's vitest. I hand-ported your diff into 2.46.7's compiled `dist/` files (`port.diff` below). Harness below.
> 
> **On multi-main**, I need to correct my earlier question after reading more closely. On a follower, `this.resuming` is empty, so the claim goes to `ResumeAttemptService.claim`. The sweep's attempt there is a counter, not a lock. With the default `N8N_EXECUTIONS_MAX_RESUME_ATTEMPTS=2`, the follower is usually granted the next attempt and resumes the parent. Two narrower gaps remain, and I found both by reading the code only (we run a single main):
> 
> * If the follower's read-then-update in `claimResumeAttempt` overlaps the sweep's claim or release UPDATE, it gets `conflict`. That becomes `ExecutionAlreadyResumingError` with `local: false`, which [fix(core): prevent parent executions from getting stuck during sub-wo… #44765](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/44765) doesn't retry, so the parent stays `waiting`. This window is about as narrow as the original one.
> * With `N8N_EXECUTIONS_MAX_RESUME_ATTEMPTS=1`, the follower gets `exhausted` instead, and the parent is marked crashed.
> 
> Would a single retry on `conflict` while the row is still `waiting` cover the first one? Happy to leave that for a follow-up issue if it's out of scope here.
> 
> Harness (compose, workflows, Dockerfile, port, driver)

Hey @dvystrcil. Thanks for the harness results — 10/90 vs 0/90 is strong validation. And you're right to correct the multi-main analysis.

On the two gaps:

1. Valid. claimResumeAttempt returns one conflict outcome for both "the row left waiting" and "the CAS on resumeAttempts lost while the row is still waiting". Only the second is retryable. A bounded retry for just that case should cover it, but it needs a distinct outcome or a re-read inside claimResumeAttempt; claimParent cannot tell the two apart today.
2. Valid and separate. With N8N_EXECUTIONS_MAX_RESUME_ATTEMPTS=1, the sweep's inspection claim can consume the only attempt, and claim() marks the parent crashed before a follower can claim. A conflict retry does not fix that; it needs separate handling.

Both are pre-existing multi-main interactions, not the single-main race this PR fixes. I'd keep #44765 scoped, add a multi-main note with these two gaps, and open a follow-up for the claim-conflict/exhaustion handling. If you'd rather fold the conflict retry into this PR, I can, but the exhaustion case would still be follow-up.

I'll open a follow-up GitHub issue covering both:

- Split conflict into "row left waiting" and "lost the resumeAttempts CAS while still waiting", and retry only the second with a bounded loop.
- Handle exhausted during the sweep's inspection so it cannot consume the final attempt and mark the parent crashed before release.

And agreed on the conflict point — the outcome name hides two very different cases. Thanks again for the harness; 10/90 vs 0/90 plus the 18 wait-path hits made the validation much stronger.
